name: Kimiko Adler
extracted_department: Kimiko Adler is a PhD student who received her BA in Classical Studies and Government from Claremont McKenna College in 2023, writing her thesis on Roman literary representations of Jews and cult of Isis devotees during the imperial period. Her research interests include the archaeology of the Roman Near East, Jewish communities under Roman rule, and cultural heritage policy. She has excavated with the Agora Valley Project at Morgantina (summer 2023) and the Gabii Project (summer 2022). Email: kja326@nyu.edu

name: Antonio Cilibrizzi
extracted_department: Antonio Cilibrizzi is a PhD student who holds a BA in Classics and German from Yale University, where he wrote a German dissertation on Goethe's Faust II and its implications for the author's Classicism. He is interested in Archaic and Early Classical Greek literature broadly, with an emphasis on social and political forms of conviviality, conceptualizations of daily life, and the emergence of prose. His secondary interests are in continental thought as it pertains to ideology and sociality. Antonio spent the summer of 2022 studying in the Classics Department at the University of Cologne and, before moving to the US, was an au pair (2018) in Nanterre, France, and an exchange student (2017) in Wuerzburg, Germany. Email: ac10640@nyu.edu

name: Hannah Cochran
extracted_department: Hannah Cochran is a PhD student who received a BA in Classical Studies and a BA in History from the University of Puget Sound in 2019, and then completed a post-baccalaureate program in Classics at the Columbia University in 2021. Her research interests include Roman history and literature, the history and reception of Alexander the Great, the memory of the Roman Republic in Imperial literature and culture, Latin epigraphy, and Augustan poetry, especially Ovid's exile poetry. As an undergraduate, she helped write entries on Pompeiian graffiti for inclusion in the Epigraphic Database Roma as part of the Ancient Graffiti Project. Email: hc3432@nyu.edu

name: Nicolette Douvas
extracted_department: Nicolette Douvas is an MA student who earned her BA in Classical Studies (concentration in Classical Languages) from Rice University (2025), with a minor in English. She then completed a Post-Baccalaureate program at Loyola University Chicago (2026). Her main research interests are in ancient Greek literature and language, particularly Greek lyric, as well as archaeology and cultural exchange in the ancient Mediterranean. Email: nd3228@nyu.edu

name: Caroline Foley
extracted_department: Caroline Foley is an MA student who received her BA in History and Classical Civilization with a minor in Ancient Greek from Boston University in 2025. Her primary interests include Greek rhetoric, classical reception in the 20th century, and the lives of women in the ancient Greek world. Email: cwf2031@nyu.edu

name: Kori Ginzberg
extracted_department: Kori Ginzberg is a PhD student who received an MA in History from Brooklyn College in 2025, an MA in Classics from Tufts University in 2019, and a BA in Political Science and in Classics from Swarthmore College in 2015. She taught middle school Latin for seven years and high school computer science for two; she has also taught public speaking and creative writing. Her major research interests include Latin epic; ancient Greek romances; queer and embodied theoretical approaches to exile, time, and environments; and medieval and modern reconstitutions of classical generic elements. Email: kjg9911@nyu.edu

name: Kathryn Hall
extracted_department: Kathryn Hall is an MA student who received her BA in classics with a minor in psychology from the University of Miami in 2025. Her interests in ancient medicine and classical philology inspired her undergraduate thesis, which conducted a close, textual analysis of the Cnidian Maxims in an attempt to understand non-Hippocratic Greek medical thought in the 5th century BCE. Kathryn hopes to continue to develop her research interests as she ultimately plans to pursue a PhD in the field. Email: kah9989@nyu.edu

name: Pei He
extracted_department: Pei He is a PhD student who received her BA in Mathematical Decision Sciences from UNC-Chapel Hill, her PhD in Statistics from Stanford University, and then her M.A. in Comparative Literature from San Francisco State University. Her MA thesis is on affect and temporality in Archaic Greek (Sappho) and Classical Chinese lyrics. While having a wide interest in lyrics, drama, and narratives of the Greco-Roman world, currently her main theoretical focus lies in how affect is evoked in ancient literary texts and how the readerly affect is triggered through the cognitive process of reading those texts. Her current CV may be found here. Email: he.pei@nyu.edu

name: Oliver Huston
extracted_department: Oliver Huston is a PhD student who received his BA and MA in Classics from Yale University (2025), where he wrote his thesis on the Italian geographical excursus in Book II of Lucan’s Bellum Civile. His research interests include Neronian literature (especially Lucan) and Classical reception in Russia. He has also excavated with the Gabii Project (2022 & 2023). Email: oh2163@nyu.edu

name: Loren Isotalo
extracted_department: Loren Isotalo is a current MA student who obtained bachelors degrees in Music and Classical Archaeology from the University of Massachusetts - Amherst before being awarded his Masters of Studies in Ancient Greek and/or History with Merit from the University of Oxford. His undergradate honors thesis and Masters dissertation both studied the ancient Greek aulos, examining first its cultural contexts in the Classical period and then its diffusion across the Mediterranean. His research interests include ancient music and dance, the archaeology of cultural heritage, and object provenance. He has excavated at Poggio Civitate Archaeological Field School (summers 2022, 2025, and 2026) and worked with the Kea Archaeological Research Survey (summer 2024). Email: lsi7118@nyu.edu

name: Mal Main
extracted_department: Mal Main is a PhD student who received their BA in Classics from the University of Kentucky and their MA in Classics from the University of Arizona. Their primary research interests include Translation Studies, Latin elegy, and the tragedies of Seneca the Younger; they have also presented research on Latin pedagogy, classical reception, and gender in antiquity. Email: mlm9673@nyu.edu

name: Alexandra McLean
extracted_department: Alexandra McLean is an MA student who earned dual BA degrees in Classics and Latin from Montclair State University (2026), with minors in both Ancient Mediterranean Civilizations and Archaeology. Her research interests include classical philology and literature, particularly Homeric language, poetics, and reception in Athenian drama; representations of death and mortality in Greek and Roman literature; and magic and ritual in the ancient world. She has excavated at the Villa Degli Antonini Research Project and Field School in Genzano di Roma, IT (2023).

name: Emma Louise Mendez Correa
extracted_department: Emma Louise Mendez Correa, who originally is from Amsterdam, is a PhD student who received her BA (2019) and research MA (2022, cum laude) in Classics from Leiden University. Her research interests mainly concern consumption and pleasure in the ancient world, with a focus on Archaic Greek poetry. She prefers to work interdisciplinarily, depending mostly on the social sciences. Next to having been part of several university-wide boards and comittees at Leiden University, she also has extensive experience in the commercial publishing industry. Email: em4811@nyu.edu

name: Stephanie Savage
extracted_department: Stephanie Savage is a PhD student who earned her MA in Classics from the University of Arizona (2019), completed a Post-Baccalaureate program at Georgetown University (2017), and earned her BA from the University of Florida (2014) in Classical Studies with minors in both Secondary Education and Anthropology. Her main research interests include the archaeology of the Peloponnese from the Bronze Age through the Hellenistic period, the development of sanctuary spaces, regional variations in culture and religious practices, the intersection of warfare and the archaeological record, and Sparta and her modern reception. She attended the American School for Classical Studies at Athens as a Regular Member last year. Email: sls994@nyu.edu

name: Poppy Steel Swayne
extracted_department: Poppy Steel Swayne is a PhD student who received her BA (2017) and MA (2019) in Classics from Durham University in the UK. Her main research interests are Greek tragedy and Greek and Roman New Comedy, as well as the ancient reception of these in Greek and Latin literature.

Miaohan (Mia) Wang is a PhD student in Classics. She received her BA in Psychology and Mathematics from New York University (2019), an MA in Computational Social Science (2021), and an MA in Humanities from the University of Chicago (2025). Her research focuses on Hellenistic philosophy and Ancient Greek medicine, with particular interest in mind–body interaction, perception, and mental illness. She has written on Senecan tragedies and Orphic beliefs for her MA thesis, and her participation in the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (Summer Seminar I, 2025) further inspired her to study the connections between philosophy, society, and the material world. Email: mw3197@nyu.edu

name: Lucy Western
extracted_department: Lucy Western is a PhD student who received her B.A. in Classics from Yale in 2019. Her primary research interests include archaic Greek lyric, contemporary reception of ancient poetic traditions, and translation.

name: Evan Wontor Shaal
extracted_department: Evan Wontor Shaal is a PhD student who received his BA in Classics with a special concentration in Medieval and Renaissance Studies from Columbia University in 2024. His senior thesis was about the nature of male/female friendships in Plautus’ Truculentus. His research interests include Roman comedy, Greek drama, both Greek and Latin epic poetry (especially Homer, Lucan, and Vergil), Augustan poetry, and Medieval and Renaissance Latin literature. Email: eaw9144@nyu.edu.

name: Joshua Williams
extracted_department: Joshua Williams is a PhD student who received a BA in Classics from the University of St. Andrews in 2018. His main interests are Archaic and Classical Greek literature, Greek religion, and ancient philosophy (especially Plato). E-mail: jjw519@nyu.edu
